tasks.instruction: in_range(x, lo, hi) should report whether x lies between lo and hi with both ends included; currently a value equal to hi is rejected.
tasks.note: Flipping the lower bound to strict as well looks symmetric but rejects x equal to lo.

tasks.instruction: sat_add(a, b) should return a + b, but when the true sum does not fit it should return the largest representable value instead of wrapping around.
tasks.note: Testing the wrapped sum with <= instead of < saturates whenever b is zero.

tasks.instruction: avg(a, b) should return the average of a and b rounded down, and must stay correct even when a + b is larger than the largest representable value.
tasks.note: Halving each operand separately avoids the overflow but drops the carry when both are odd.

tasks.instruction: page_count(items, per_page) should return how many pages are needed to show all items (per_page is at least 1), counting a partially filled last page as a page.
tasks.note: Adding per_page instead of per_page minus one gives an extra page whenever items divide evenly.

tasks.instruction: prev_slot(i, n) gives the slot before i in a ring of n slots numbered 0 to n-1; stepping back from slot 0 should land on the last slot.
tasks.note: Wrapping with a remainder of i-1 looks right but i-1 wraps to the maximum value first, which only lands on n-1 for powers of two.

tasks.instruction: clamp_index(i, len) should return i when it is a valid index of a list of len elements (len at least 1), and otherwise the last valid index.
tasks.note: Also relaxing the guard to i <= len lets i equal to len through unchanged.

tasks.instruction: grade(score) returns 3 for scores of 90 and above, 2 for scores of 80 and above, otherwise 1; a score of exactly 90 currently gets the wrong grade.
tasks.note: Making both thresholds use the same strictness, or lowering the constant, changes the score-80 or score-89 boundary.

tasks.instruction: count_above(values, t) should count the entries of values that are strictly greater than t; entries equal to t must not be counted.
tasks.note: Writing the comparison as t > value counts entries below the threshold instead.

tasks.instruction: remaining(total, used) returns how much of total is left after used; when used exceeds total the answer should be 0 rather than a huge wrapped number.
tasks.note: Writing the overflow test as total > used swaps the operands and zeroes every normal case.

tasks.instruction: ring_distance(head, tail, n) gives how many steps forward from tail reach head in a ring of n slots (head and tail are below n); it is wrong when head is behind tail.
tasks.note: Computing tail minus head reads naturally as a distance but measures the opposite direction.

tasks.instruction: bit_field(x, pos, width) should return the width bits of x starting at bit position pos as a small number (width between 1 and 31); it currently also returns all the bits above the field.
tasks.note: Shifting width left by one instead of one left by width builds a wrong mask.

tasks.instruction: budget_left(limit, spent, refund) returns what remains of limit after spending, never going below 0; the refund amount should be added to the limit before spending is taken off.
tasks.note: Passing the spent amount as the first argument of the saturating helper subtracts in the wrong direction.

tasks.instruction: sat_mul(a, b) should return a times b, or the largest representable value when the true product does not fit.
tasks.note: Reusing the addition overflow check (result smaller than an operand) misses many wrapped products.

tasks.instruction: elapsed(start, now) returns ticks passed on a free-running counter that wraps from the largest value back to 0; when now is below start the counter has wrapped and the result should be the ticks actually passed, not 0.
tasks.note: Adding the distance to the top and the distance from zero forgets the tick from the maximum value to 0.

tasks.instruction: checksum(v) should be the wrapping sum of each entry times its position plus one, over all six entries; the last entry is currently left out.
tasks.note: Raising the count one past the length re-reads the first entry because indexes wrap around.

tasks.instruction: low_byte_bits(x) should count how many of the eight lowest bits of x are set; the highest of those eight bits is currently ignored.
tasks.note: Counting nine positions includes bit 8, which lies outside the low byte.
